uncertain.why: Bold «(جَامِعَ عوالمي)»: only ONE kasra is printed, under the vertical lam-mim-ya ligature (component analysis at 1300-1800 dpi). It cannot be resolved whether it belongs to the lam or to the mim. Written on the mim, because this text regularly vowels the letter before a final ي. Expected عَوَالِمِي.

print_errors.note: The ayah-end ornament after 48:1 is printed with ٢ instead of ١. The next ornament (after مُّسْتَقِيمًا) is also ٢. Checked at 1000 dpi. Kept as printed.
No sukun on the lam, and the shadda on the yeh has no fatha (component map at 2000 dpi). Expected الْقُدُّوسِيَّةِ. Kept as printed.
There is a kasra under the heh and no fatha above it. The nun carries a fatha, and the zay carries shadda+fatha (component map at 1600 dpi). Expected الْمُنَزَّهَةِ. Kept as printed.
The bold initial waw has no fatha (checked at 1600 dpi), unlike (وَاحْمِلْنِي) etc. Kept. The same applies to (وانْشُلْنِي) on the same page.
No spaces are printed between ﴾ and [, or between ]. and (. The gap ﴾→[ is 26 px at 1000 dpi, where spaced cases on the same page are 67-89 px. Kept glued.

In bold «(وَاجْعَلِ الْحِجَابَ الَأْعْظَمَ)», the marks on the lam-alif are swapped: a fatha sits over the lam stroke, and a round sukun sits over the hamza on the alif stroke. Compare the correct bold الْأَحَدِيَّةِ (p.062) and الْأَوَّلِ (p.064), where the sukun is over the lam stroke and the fatha over the hamza. Kept as printed.
أي is printed with a dotless ى (footnote 1). A stray space is printed before the final period («وظهور .», a 44 px gap at 1000 dpi). It was normalized per CONVENTIONS §2.

A wide space (justified, about 170 px at 1000 dpi) is printed between أَمْرِنَا and ﴾. It was normalized to no space per §2. ﴾ and [ are printed glued (27 px) and kept glued. The same glued ﴾[ is kept in «نَّفْسِكَ﴾[النساء: ٧٩]» (24 px).

The Quran quotation in footnote 1 is set in bold naskh, not the mushaf font. It is transcribed with its printed marks: no silent-zero on تُوَلُّوا, and no case vowel on الله (the font's ligature only). scripts/quran.py flags both against Tanzil, as expected.
Both are printed with fatha on the mim and a sukun on the ain (مَعْ), not مَعَ. Component maps at 800 dpi. Kept as printed.
Shadda+damma is printed on the initial mim (expected مُؤَزَّرًا). Kept as printed.
A visible gap is printed before ﴾ (120 px and 68 px at 1000 dpi). It was normalized to no space per §2.

notes: Markers: p.061 continues p.060 mid-sentence (p.060 ends «مِن رَّفِيعِ الرُّتْبَةِ», and p.061 begins «وَعَظِيمِ الْمَنْزِلَةِ»). p.062 continues the hadith «إِنَّمَا | بُعِثْتُ». p.063 and p.064 also begin mid-sentence, so all four pages get '+'. No footnote continues across pages. Paragraphs: on p.061 a new indented paragraph starts at «الْخَاضِعُ» after «[الفتح: ١-٣].», and p.062 is one paragraph. On p.063 a new indented paragraph starts at «(وَرُوحَهُ)». On p.064 one starts at «(يَا أَوَّلُ)» after «[آل عمران: ٨١].». Bold: the bold Mashishiyya phrases and the bold hadith texts are wrapped (**…**) and «**…**», with the light-weight parentheses and quotes outside, as in keyA b15. The bold spans that cross a line join into one span. The hadith «إِنَّمَا بُعِثْتُ…» crosses the page break, so it is closed at the end of p.061 and reopened on p.062. «(وَرُوحَهُ)» on p.063 is bold (checked at 1000 dpi). The hadith «كُنْتُ أَوَّلَ النَّاسِ…» on p.064 is in regular weight, as is «جَيْشِ» between two bold spans on p.062. Lam-mim and lam-ha mark clusters were resolved by connected-component analysis (BFS labelling, colour maps under scratch\a16). In the regular font at 1600 dpi, sukun alone measures about 74x55 / 2200 px, sukun+fatha about 90x86 / 3000, and sukun+damma about 97x94 / 3450. This gives الْمَنْزِلَةِ (p.061: sukun+fatha over lam, plus a separate sukun for the nun), الْمَسَالِكِ, الْمُحِيطَةِ, الْمُوقِعَةِ, الْمُنَزَّهِةِ, and الْكَثْرَةِ (sukun alone, then fatha on kaf). In bold, the 'hat' cluster (81x78 / 2486, identical to الْجَامِعُ on p.060) is sukun+fatha: الْجَهْلِ, الْحَقِّ. A lone damma with an open loop means no sukun on the lam: الجِسْمَانِيِّ (nothing on the lam), القُدُّوسِيّةِ, and المُجَسِّمة in the p.062 footnote. In the footnote, الْمُوَصِّلُ (p.063 fn 3) has a filled sukun+damma cluster. وَالتَّلْقِينُ (p.063) has a sukun on the lam and a plain kasra on the qaf, with no shadda. Quran: the encoding follows Tanzil, with the dagger alif written directly after the letter. The upright rectangular zero ۠ on أَنَا۠ (12:108) was distinguished from the round zero ۟ on أَدْعُوٓا۟ by direct shape comparison: an upright oval with a tall flat-bottomed hole, versus a tilted round zero. The blue small-jim ۚ (12:108) and the صلى signs ۖ (42:11, 4:79, 32:24) are printed and kept. The quote-final waqf signs that Tanzil has (12:108, 2:197, 4:78, 4:79, 42:52, 2:30, 3:81, 3:160) are not printed and are not added; scripts/quran.py flags these as quran_marks only. Hamza seats follow Tanzil: أَئِمَّةً has its hamza drawn below the tooth, and بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا has the hamza on a kashida seat. ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ keeps Tanzil's tatweel + small high yeh. Spacing: '[الفتح: ١-٣]' has no spaces around the dash. Digit-gap measurements show the gaps equal the digits' own side-bearings, as in «١٠٧». '[الإسراء:١]' is printed with no space after the colon. On p.062, ﴾→[ before [محمد: ٢١] is 45 px against 26 px glued, so it is kept with a space. On p.064, ﴾→[ before [آل عمران: ١٦٠] is also 45 px and kept with a space. «]،﴿وَمَا» (p.062) has a 48 px gap, the same as the glued «]،﴿مَّن» on p.060 (42 px), so it is kept glued. The name الله: with a printed case vowel over the font ligature it is written as in keyA b13-b15 (no explicit shadda). The bold «(اللَّهُمَّ…)» on p.061 has an explicit shadda+fatha on the lam (component map) and is written with all its marks. Final ى: the small alif over final ى on these pages is the font's (none of pp.061-064 is in ref\typed_dagger_pages.json), so it is written plain (حَتَّى، عَلَى، الهَوَى، تَرَدَّى، تعالى، تجلى). On p.064, «(يَا أَوَّلُ)…» is in a tight font. Normal word spaces are written, as the print gives no other evidence. validate.py prints OK.
